newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK INDUSTRY'S PROFITS ROSE MODESTLY IN 96 - SEV.
newsitem.headline: GREEK INDUSTRY'S PROFITS ROSE MODESTLY IN 96 - SEV.

text.p: The Greek industry posted modest profits in 1995 compared to 1994 and profitable firms in 1994 saw their profits rise 13 percent in 1995, the Federation of Greek Industries (SEV) said in a statement.
The increase was mainly the result of a fall in interest expenses, a trend which is not likely to continue at the same pace over the next years, it said.
The 1995 ICAP survey of Greek industrial firms included both profitable and money-losing firms and its profitability and return-on-equity indicators were not representative, it said.
"The ICAP 1995 survey on Greek industry profits includes the income statements of companies which incurred losses on that particular year," the statement said.
"Even if these companies have lessened their losses, they cannot serve as an indicator of the profitability of the whole Greek industry sector," the statement added.
The 1995 pre-tax ROE of the profitable industry was down to 18.5 percent from 19.9 percent in 1994. The after-tax ROE was almost the same with that of tax-free bond yields, it added.
The decrease in pre-tax ROE in the 1994-95 period was due to the substantial increase in the industry's equity capital.
"This is a healthy investment move in itself," the statement said.
